text.p: LME lead took a beating on Tuesday afternoon as U.S.-based speculative selling knocked it to the lowest in 22 months. But aside from aluminium, which settled slightly weaker in a correction, the other metals ended the day within recent ranges after seeing fairly light turnover.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 1.66 points to 243.60.

On the LME, lead lost ground in the morning, then during lunchtime U.S. funds unleashed the selling, dealers said. The three months market has looked wobby over the past few days, failing on Friday to sustain the $640 per tonne mark. Short selling pushed prices still lower, triggering stop-loss selling on the way down. It bottomed at a low of $603, the weakest since June 1995. Prices tried to bounce, but finished the afternoon kerb near the lows at $605, a loss of $32 or five percent.

Aluminium etched out a new range after a correction on the pre-market knocked it from a fresh high of $1,747 on Monday. Prices edged down to a low of $1,712, but closed the day with pared losses of $23 at $1,721.
Three months zinc took a stab at the $1,500 level, scoring a high of $1,502, but failed to sustain it, ending the day $4 higher at $1,498.

Copper consolidated in a narrow range below $2,300, finding a comfortable region and confounding analysts which keep expecting it to visit the downside as stocks continue to build. Three months closed the kerb $3 firmer at $2,282.
Nickel came off its morning low of $7,180, finishing the day $45 stronger at $7,260.

IPE September Brent futures closed a few cents firmer on Tuesday after last minute buying ahead of the release of API data pushed the contract out of the day's narrow range. September Brent closed at $19.54 a barrel, up eight cents on the day and just four cents off the days high of $19.58 which was reached just before the close.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a wheat estimate by Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies, traders said. Sources said Sparks estimated 1997 U.S. total wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, above USDA's July outlook for 2.431 billion. Also Sparks tabbed 1997-98 U.S. wheat ending stocks at 861 million bushels, above USDA's July forecast for ending stocks at 650 million, sources said. CBOT SRW wheat closed 1-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down 1-1/2 at $3.53-1/4.

COMEX gold and silver futures ended sharply lower Tuesday, but platinum group metals (PGM) futures held up well with new contract highs in platinum and palladium ended up by the daily limit for the third straight day. "We think gold is going lower," Chicago Corp's COMEX floor trader Carlos Perez-Santalla said. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $320.20/70, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $321.10 and the New York close Monday at $323.65/15.
